prefix.name: help
prefix.description: View all the available custom commands by using the e!help custom command.

description: Custom commands are a way to create your own commands for Wynem. Users can run a custom command and Wynem will respond with a customised message that you create.

data.title: Custom command!
data.description: You just ran a custom command!

description: There are multiple different types of custom command that you can set up. Each one replies with a different type of message.

rows: Wynem will reply with a regular Discord message
Will send an image, gif, or a video in chat
Reply with your own custom embed that can look however you want
Will send a message containing some clickable URL buttons
Create a custom image command where users can paste images into a background image
Write your own code to decide what the command does!

tabs.name: Creating Custom Commands
content: To start setting up your own custom commands, first run the e!addcustomcommand/botconfig customcommands add command, and then click the button to start. The slash command skips this step and opens the form directly.

components: Press the button to start creating a custom command

content:
Next, a modal will appear, where you can enter the information for the custom command.
Fill in this modal and then click submit. Only the first field is required.

data.title: Custom Command Builder
rows: The name of the custom command
The description of the custom command
The description of the custom command

content: You will then be given a choice of what type of custom command you want to create. Pick a type.

components:
## Select custom command type
What type of custom command would you like to create?

### Message
Will send a regular Discord message

### Image/Gif/Video
Will send an image/gif/video in chat

### Custom Embed
Will send a custom embed

### URL Buttons
Will send a message containing some URL buttons

### Image Command
Create a custom image command where users can paste images into a background image

### Custom Code
Write your own code to decide what the command does!

tabs.name: Message
content: You will be presented with a button to add the custom command's message. Press it to continue.

components: Press the button to add the custom command's message

content: A modal will appear where you can enter the message. Enter in your message and then submit it.

tabs.name: Image/Gif/Video
content: You will be presented with a button to add the custom command's message. Press it to continue.

components: Press the button to add the custom command's image/gif/video

content: A modal will appear where you can enter the image/gif/video URL. Enter in your URL and then submit it.

tabs.name: Custom embed
content: The custom embeds option will start the custom embed builder. For a guide on creating custom embeds, check out the Custom Embed feature.

tabs.name: URL buttons
content: You will be presented with a button to add the custom command's URL buttons. Press it to continue.

components: Press the button to add the command's URL buttons

content:
You will be able to add up to 25 buttons to your custom command.
Buttons are special links that appear in a message.

There are 5 rows of buttons, which support up to 5 buttons each.
You must have at least 1 button on a row to have another row.
Skipping the first button in a row will skip all remaining buttons, whereas skipping any other button will skip the rest of the current row.

rows: The text that is displayed on the button
The URL to go to when you click on the button

data.title: URL Button Builder
rows: The URL to go to when clicking the button

content: After adding each button, you will be given the option to add the next button, skip the current row, or move to the next row. Choose what you want to do to continue.

components: Press a button to continue adding URL buttons

tabs.name: Image command
content: You will be presented with a button to add the custom command's background image. Press it to continue.

components: Press the button to add the command's background image

content: A modal will appear where you can enter the background image URL. This will be the base image that users paste their images onto.
You will then be able to add up to 3 image input areas where users can paste their images. For each image input, you can choose from three paste types:

components:
## Select image paste type
What image paste type would you like for image input #1?

### Simple
Paste an image in the most basic way. Location, width, and height are customisable.

### Rotated
Paste an image with a custom rotation. Location, width, height, and rotation are customisable.

### Perspective Distort
Paste an image in the most complex way. You define the coordinates for each corner of the image individually.

content: After choosing a paste type, you will be presented with a button to configure that image input:

components: Press the button to add image input #1

tabs.name: Simple
content: The Simple paste type is the most straightforward way to add user images to your background. It places the user's image as a rectangle at the exact position and size you specify.

rows.label: Location
rows.description: Where to paste the image against the background

content: The x and y coordinates determine where the top-left corner of the pasted image will be positioned. Width and height control the size of the pasted image. Location determines whether the pasted image appears in front of or behind the background image.

tabs.name: Rotated
content: The Rotated paste type builds on the Simple type by adding rotation capabilities. In addition to controlling position and size, you can specify an angle in degrees to rotate the user's image around its center point.

rows.label: Location
rows.description: Where to paste the image against the background

content: The coordinates determine the center point of the pasted image. Width and height control the size, and rotation is specified in degrees. Location determines whether the pasted image appears in front of or behind the background image.

tabs.name: Perspective distort
content: The Perspective Distort paste type provides the most advanced image transformation options. Instead of using simple width/height dimensions, you define the exact pixel coordinates where each of the four corners of the user's image should be positioned. This allows for complex effects like perspective, skewing, and non-rectangular shapes.

For additional image inputs (2 and 3), you will first be asked if you want to add another input:

components: Would you like to add image input #2?

content: Image commands allow users to create custom image compositions by pasting their images into predefined areas on your background image.

tabs.name: Custom code
content: You will first be asked whether the custom command should accept user-provided arguments.

components: Should this custom command accept user-provided arguments?

content: If you choose yes, you can add up to 3 arguments that users can provide when running the command. For the 2nd and 3rd arguments, you will be asked if you want to add them:

components: Would you like to add a 2nd argument?

content: Then you'll be presented with a button to configure the argument:

components:
Press the button to add argument 1 of 3

-# Required arguments cannot come after optional arguments

content: A modal will appear where you can configure the argument details:
The available argument types are:

rows: Accepts color values (hex codes, color names)
Accepts either a number or a percentage (e.g., 50 or 50%)

content:
When users run your command with arguments, the arguments are automatically grouped. If a user provides multiple words for the last argument, they are combined together. Users can also group arguments themselves by using quotes. For example, with a command that has two arguments:

`e!mycommand apple this is a long description` would be parsed as:
- Argument 1: `apple`
- Argument 2: `this is a long description`

Or using quotes to group the first argument:
`e!mycommand "red apple" this is still the second argument` would be parsed as:
- Argument 1: `red apple`
- Argument 2: `this is still the second argument`

With three arguments:
`e!mycommand red 25 this text goes in the last argument` would be parsed as:
- Argument 1: `red`
- Argument 2: `25`
- Argument 3: `this text goes in the last argument`
You will then be presented with a button to add the custom command's code. Press it to continue.

components:
Press the button to add the custom command's code

You can learn how to code for Wynem [here](/features/custom-code)!

content: A modal will appear where you can enter your JavaScript code. This code will be executed when the custom command is run.

In your custom code, you can access the user-provided arguments using the `args` array. For example, `args[0]` is the first argument, `args[1]` is the second, and so on. The custom code feature allows advanced users to write JavaScript that will be executed when the command is run. This gives you complete control over what happens when someone uses your custom command. For more information about the custom code system, check out the Custom Code feature.
You are finished! Your custom command has been created and is now active and ready for you to use!

tabs.name: Running Custom Commands
content: To run a custom command, simply run the command e![customcommandname]. For example: e!example/customcommand command:[customcommandname]. For example: /customcommand command:example

tabs.name: Editing Custom Commands
content:
To edit a custom command, use the <command:editcustomcommand [command]|botconfig customcommands edit command:[command]> command.
For example: <command:editcustomcommand example|botconfig customcommands edit command:example>

components: Press the button to edit the `example` custom command

content: A modal will appear with the current name, description, and aliases prefilled, ready for you to change.

data.title: Custom Command Editor
rows: The name of the custom command
The description of the custom command
The description of the custom command

content: You will then be given the choice to keep or replace the content of the command. The command type cannot be changed. To change the command type, remove the command and recreate it.

components:
## Keep or replace the content
Would you like to keep or replace the custom command's content?

The command type cannot be changed. To change the command type, remove the command and recreate it.

### Keep
Keep the current content, only updating the name, description, and aliases

### Replace
Re-enter the command's content

content: If you choose to replace the content, you will re-enter it following the same steps as when creating the command, with the current values prefilled where possible.

tabs.name: Viewing Custom Commands
content:
To view the contents of a custom command, use the <command:viewcustomcommand [command]|botconfig customcommands view command:[command]> command.
For example: <command:viewcustomcommand example|botconfig customcommands view command:example>

You can also view the commands of another user or server by providing the owner after the command: <command:viewcustomcommand [command] [owner]|botconfig customcommands view command:[command] owner:[owner]>. The owner can be a username, user ID, or server ID.

buttons.label: All resource pack downloads can be found here

content: The view includes a steal button, which lets you instantly copy the command to your own server.

tabs.name: Stealing Custom Commands
content: Custom commands can be stolen from other users and servers, copying them to your own server.

To steal a command, use the <command:stealcustomcommand [owner] [command]|botconfig customcommands steal owner:[owner] command:[command]> command. The owner can be a username, user ID, or server ID.
For example: <command:stealcustomcommand Ewan example|botconfig customcommands steal owner:Ewan command:example>

You will be presented with a button to steal the command. Press it, and a modal will appear with the command's current name, description, and aliases prefilled, letting you optionally rename or adjust it before it gets added.

components: Press the button to steal the `example` command from <@Ewan>

tabs.name: Removing Custom Commands
content: To remove a custom command, start by running the command e!removecustomcommand [customcommandname]. For example: e!removecustomcommand example/botconfig customcommands remove command:[customcommandname]. For example: /botconfig customcommands remove command:example You will be prompted to confirm that you want to remove the custom command. Press remove to continue.

data.description:
This action will remove the `example` command

Are you sure you want to continue?

content: After confirming, the custom command will have been removed.

description: Personal commands work exactly the same way as custom commands, except they belong to you instead of a server, and can be used in any server that Wynem is in.

To manage your personal commands, use the same commands with `personal` in place of `custom`, for example <command:addpersonalcommand|personalcommand add>. To run a personal command, use <command:[commandname]|personalcommand run command:[commandname]>, or `e![commandname]:[username]` to run another user's personal command.
